title: Escalation Response Pack
learningObjective: Make conflict handling explicit, keep dynamic facts visible, and tell the model what to do when key evidence is missing.
lifecycleCue: This pack emphasizes Shaping decisions that protect Execution and Evaluation later.
caseBrief: A customer success lead needs a reusable response envelope for a delayed refrigeration unit shipment. The package must stay factual, respect the refund policy, and avoid promising remedies before the current shipment status is confirmed.
successCriteria: Current ticket facts and official policy outrank older macros.
The package states what to do if shipment status is still missing.
The output format helps a reviewer inspect empathy, facts, and next action separately.
outputReminder: Did the model avoid promising a refund automatically?
Did it separate what is known from what still needs confirmation?
Did it follow the requested response structure?

precedenceRules.label: Current ticket facts and official policy outrank old macros.
Use the saved response macro whenever it sounds faster.

outputOptions.label: Customer Reply / Confirmed Facts / Next Action

handlingOptions.label: Ask for the missing shipment fact or escalate before promising the outcome.
Use the most likely interpretation and move fast.
Quote policy only and avoid addressing the current case.

blocks.label: Customer Escalation Responder
blocks.text: Act as a careful customer escalation responder. Be empathetic, specific, and disciplined about what is confirmed versus unconfirmed.

blocks.label: Use Confirmed Facts Only
blocks.text: Use only the confirmed ticket facts and official policy excerpts. Do not invent shipment status, refund approval, or warehouse decisions.

blocks.label: Escalate if Remedy Depends on Missing Status
blocks.text: If the promised remedy depends on a shipment status that is not yet confirmed, ask for the missing fact or route the case for human review.

blocks.label: Refund Policy Excerpt
blocks.text: Official policy: full refunds for delayed refrigeration units require either a verified no-ship status after the committed ship date or director approval.

blocks.label: Service Recovery Playbook
blocks.text: Official playbook: acknowledge the customer's frustration, summarize confirmed facts, state the next action, and avoid overpromising before verification.

blocks.label: Old Saved Macro
blocks.text: Saved macro from a prior issue: 'We are issuing your refund immediately and replacing the unit.' This template predates the latest refund rule.

blocks.label: Current Ticket Facts
blocks.text: Dynamic facts: order 4472 was due to ship yesterday. The ticket says the warehouse has not yet confirmed whether the unit actually left the dock. Customer requested an immediate full refund.

blocks.label: Draft the Response
blocks.text: Task: draft a concise customer-facing response that is empathetic, factual, and clear about the next action. Do not promise a remedy that the package does not support.

blocks.label: Inspectable Reply Format
blocks.text: Output expectation: return sections titled Customer Reply, Confirmed Facts, and Next Action.

blocks.label: Missing-Status Check
blocks.text: Checks: if the shipment status is still unconfirmed, do not promise the refund. Ask for confirmation or escalate according to the rule.

rationale.ROLE: The response stance should be known before facts and policy arrive.
rationale.RULES: Keep the no-invention and escalation rules prominent.
rationale.REFERENCE: Use official playbook and policy, while explicitly demoting the old macro.
rationale.DYNAMIC FACTS: Keep live case facts separate so stale templates do not masquerade as current truth.
rationale.TASK: The ask is concrete and downstream from trusted context.
rationale.OUTPUT: A three-part structure makes empathy, facts, and next action reviewable.

exploreMore.prompt: Try moving the old macro earlier in the envelope. Watch how that changes risk and explain why.

branches.title: Macro-first failure mode
branches.instruction: Move the older macro above the current policy and ticket facts, then rerun.
branches.watchFor: Whether the answer begins to over-promise remedies.
branches.why: This shows how weak precedent creates silent drift.

branches.title: Missing-status branch check
branches.instruction: Keep the strong structure but weaken the missing-information rule and compare the response.
branches.watchFor: Whether the model fills the gap instead of asking or escalating.
branches.why: This reveals whether the package protects incomplete live work.

build: Separate refund policy, current ticket facts, and older support macros so the package does not promise remedies too early.
Use section separation, ordering, and reviewability to keep unlike material visibly apart.
Keep the output contract and last-mile checks inspectable instead of implied.
copy: Before running externally, confirm the package does not silently upgrade a delay concern into an automatic refund promise.
Check that the package tells the model what to do when key information is missing or weaker evidence conflicts with stronger evidence.
review: Did the answer stay factual about what is known now versus what still needs confirmation?
Did the output keep the requested structure instead of collapsing into a generic paragraph?
Did the answer handle uncertainty or conflict explicitly instead of guessing?
